study_name.evidence_quote: Adrian Tett ... Cell Host & Microbe 26, 666–679, November 13, 2019
study_name.notes: Derived using common LastNameInitial_Year convention from first author 'Tett' and publication year 2019; not explicitly stated as a 'study_name' in the paper.

subject_id.notes: No individual subject identifiers are given; only aggregate cohort statistics (n, mean age, sex %) are reported.

sample_id.notes: No individual sample identifiers are reported in the main text; sample-level metadata may exist in Table S1/S2/S5 (not provided).

pmid.notes: PMID taken from paper_id provided with the input; not stated verbatim within the paper body.

subcohort.evidence_quote: For Ghana, 44 individuals were included (23 adults ... 25 children ...)

target_condition.evidence_quote: All individuals sampled in this study were healthy defined as free of self-reported disease.
target_condition.notes: These non-Westernized cohorts (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania) were sampled as healthy individuals for microbiome/P. copri characterization, not for a specific disease phenotype.

control.evidence_quote: All individuals sampled in this study were healthy defined as free of self-reported disease.
control.notes: Inferred as 'Study Control' because subjects are described as healthy volunteers, not disease cases.

country.evidence_quote: All subjects enrolled in this study included infants and adults from Ghana, Tanzania and Ethiopia

body_site.evidence_quote: Faecal samples from a Ghanaian cohort

lifestyle.evidence_quote: the local occupation is subsistence farming and the wider economy based on farming cash crops such as cocoa and plantain
lifestyle.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets
lifestyle.notes: Inferred 'Agriculturalist' lifestyle category for Ghana and Tanzania based on described subsistence farming/agriculture-based economies; Ethiopia cohort occupation not detailed.

location.evidence_quote: In Ghana 12 extended families from the Asante Akim North district region were sampled
location.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets

westernized.evidence_quote: We also sequenced two non-Westernized populations from Ghana and Tanzania.
westernized.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets
westernized.notes: Ethiopia, Ghana, and Tanzania cohorts are all classified as non-Westernized in this study.

dna_extraction_kit.evidence_quote: For all samples DNA was extracted using the PowerSoil DNA isolation kit (Qiagen)
dna_extraction_kit.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets

ncbi_accession.evidence_quote: Raw sequencing data (Ghana) This study NCBI-SRA BioProject: PRJNA529124
ncbi_accession.notes: Accessions correspond to whole cohorts (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania), not individual samples.

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: sequenced on the Illumina HiSeq2500 100nt paired end platform with a target depth of 5Gb/sample
sequencing_platform.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets

age.notes: Values are cohort mean ages (with SD/range reported), not individual ages; granularity is subgroup-level (adult/child per country).

age_group.notes: Reported ranges (e.g., Ghana children 0-15 yrs; Tanzania children 0-18 yrs; Ethiopia infants 0.167-4.5 yrs) span multiple schema age_group categories (Infant/Child/Adolescent); mapped to closest label used in paper.

ancestry.evidence_quote: infants and adults from Ghana, Tanzania and Ethiopia
ancestry.notes: Ancestry not explicitly stated; inferred broad 'African' category based on country of residence/sampling (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania).

family.evidence_quote: In Ghana 12 extended families from the Asante Akim North district region were sampled
family.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets
family.notes: Number of families reported, but individual family identifiers/linkage per sample not given in main text.

family_role.evidence_quote: This cohort included 24 mothers and their infant(s) for a total of 50 metagenomes.
family_role.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets
family_role.notes: Ghana and Tanzania cohorts described as extended families with adults/children, but explicit mother/father/child roles not specified for these two cohorts.

sex.notes: Sex reported as aggregate percentages per subgroup rather than a single categorical value per individual; cannot be reduced to a single enum value (Female/Male) without losing information. Children/infant sex composition not reported.

age_min.notes: Range given per subgroup (adults/children/infants) for each of the three newly sequenced non-Westernized cohorts (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania).

age_max.notes: Range given per subgroup for each country cohort.

age_years.evidence_quote: avg age (yrs): 33.14 (s.d.: 6.61), range: 20-45, sex: 52.2% female, 47.8% male
age_years.notes: Average (mean) age reported per subgroup, not per-sample; study reports aggregate statistics only.

bmi.evidence_quote: we considered if the P. copri complex could be associated with other factors such as body mass index (BMI) or age
bmi.section: Results — Associating P. copri Clades with Metagenomically Investigated Human Diseases
bmi.notes: BMI categories mentioned as a covariate analyzed in Table S1 but no specific BMI values reported in main text for participants.

disease.evidence_quote: All individuals sampled in this study were healthy defined as free of self-reported disease.
disease.notes: Applies uniformly to Ghana, Ethiopia, and Tanzania cohorts newly sequenced in this study. Separately, isolate genomes were sourced from 'healthy subjects and new onset rheumatoid arthritis patients' (Method Details), but demographic data for these isolate donors were not reported.

disease_details.evidence_quote: P. copri strains were isolated from stool from healthy subjects and new onset rheumatoid arthritis patients.
disease_details.section: Method Details — Constructing a P. copri Genome Panel
disease_details.notes: This refers to the source population for isolate sequencing (not the Ghana/Ethiopia/Tanzania demographic cohorts, which were healthy); no per-subject demographic data provided for RA patients.

biomarker_name.notes: No clinical biomarker measurements reported in this microbial genomics study.

disease_response_os.notes: Study does not involve survival outcomes; it is a microbial genomics/population structure study.

ecog_performance_status.notes: No clinical performance status data reported.

feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal samples were used for metagenomic sequencing, but no quantitative 'feces phenotype' values (e.g., consistency scores) were reported.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: CRC datasets were used only for microbial abundance/prevalence meta-analysis; no tumor size measurements reported.

value: P. copri complex comprises four clades (A, B, C, D)
1,023 total P. copri genomes reconstructed (17 isolates + 1,006 MAGs)
6,874 metagenomes from 36 datasets across 25 countries analyzed
Non-Westernized populations sampled: Ghana (44 metagenomes), Ethiopia (50 metagenomes), Tanzania (68 metagenomes), Madagascar (110 metagenomes)
Ancient samples: Iceman (5,300-year-old ice mummy) and 3 Mexican coprolites (~1,300 BP)
Clade divergence estimated ~6.5 million years ago (clade B split); clades A, D, C diversified ~3.5-2.5 million years ago
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: we obtained >1,000 genomes and explored the genetic and population structure of P. copri
uncurated_metadata.notes: Study is a microbial genomics/population genetics analysis, not a clinical study; most schema fields (biomarkers, OS, ECOG, tumor size) are not applicable and not reported.

host_species.evidence_quote: Prevotella copri is a common human gut microbe
host_species.notes: Study includes human fecal/gut metagenomic samples from multiple countries and ancient human remains.

extraction_warnings: This paper (Tett et al., 2019) is a genomic/metagenomic population-structure study of Prevotella copri, not a sample-metadata-centric paper; individual-level subject_id/sample_id fields are not reported in the main text.

Only aggregate demographic statistics (n, mean age ± SD, age range, % sex) are given for the three newly sequenced non-Westernized cohorts (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania), split by adult/child(infant) subgroup — treated here as subgroup_level granularity.

The vast majority of the >6,500 publicly available metagenomes analyzed in this study (from 36 datasets/25 countries) are not described with per-sample demographic details in the provided text; only summary counts are given (see Table S1/S2, not included in provided text).
study_name and pmid were derived/taken from external convention and the provided paper_id respectively, not from verbatim text within the paper body.
Sex, age_group, and family_role fields required approximations/derivations from aggregate percentages and cohort descriptions; true individual-level values are not available.

This paper is primarily a comparative genomics/metagenomics study of Prevotella copri across many public datasets (CRC, T2D, IBD, etc.) but does not report participant-level clinical metadata (disease, treatment, staging) for those cohorts in the provided text; only aggregate demographic data (age) for the three newly sequenced non-Westernized cohorts (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania) were available.

Age data are reported as subgroup-level aggregates (mean, SD, range) by country and age category (adult/child/infant), not as per-sample values, so granularity was set to subgroup_level rather than sample_level.
Disease status 'Healthy' applies uniformly across the three demographic subgroups' countries but not by age-subgroup distinctly; treated as study-wide within these subgroups.
Isolate donor disease status (rheumatoid arthritis) mentioned in Methods is not linked to specific demographic/age data and could not be mapped to any subgroup with confidence.
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('subgroup_level'); kept batch 0.
Batch 2 subgroups [] differ from batch 0 ['Ghana_adults', 'Ghana_children', 'Ethiopia_adults', 'Ethiopia_infants', 'Tanzania_adults', 'Tanzania_children']; kept batch 0.

This paper is a microbial genomics/metagenomics study of Prevotella copri population structure and does not report clinical biomarkers, overall survival, ECOG performance status, tumor size, or feces phenotype scores as defined by the schema.
Most schema fields are clinical/oncology-oriented and not applicable to this microbiome evolutionary biology paper; they are marked not_reported.

Demographic data on age/sex for non-Westernized cohorts (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania) are present in Experimental Model and Subject Details section but do not map to biomarker or disease response fields in this schema.
